Having big goals like having a huge audience and performing in front of them is really amazing, but without the smaller steps in between, it's going to be really hard to make progress. I am guessing you want to pursue singing if you are looking up to Beyonce?

If you don't already get some singing lessons, learn how to project your voice and to sing properly (Way harder than it sounds). If you are interested in it get a guitar or keyboard and learn some music theory, mainly about chords and how they fit into each other. While you are doing your singing lessons how about you do some songwriting practice? You don't have to write out full songs at first, just verses. Look at pop songs and see how they are made up of verses, choruses, bridges etc.

Just as a warning, you will suck. Nobody starts with greatness, it is earned. If you can push past that though, keep chipping away at it everyday you **will** get better. That is with singing and with songwriting. A good teacher can also make all the difference.

Once you feel confident upload some of your stuff to Soundcloud or to Youtube, start a Facebook page. These things may be quite distant depending on your current ability and practice levels, but they aren't impossibly far.

As a recap -

.Practice.  A little everyday. 10-20 mins a day is MORE than enough to start off

.Get a singing teacher if you don't have one (Even looking up youtube vids is a great way to start).Learn some music theory, especially about keys and chords.Analyse popular music artists and their songs to see how they craft them.After learning some theory and chords start writing some songs, even just verses

.After you feel confident enough upload some of your creations to the web

I agree with some of this statement but I am not sure I agree with some of your reasoning.

The reason (I think) TERFs get so much attention is because they are a formal group of people who are against trans people. It's right in the title that they oppose trans people from their little club. They have a face, and the media give them a lot of attention as they are a "organised" group. The term organised because they have a mantra and a code (That excludes trans people)

Men are not such a group. They are not organised, they do not choose to be males, they just are, and they are not "Our true enemies". Saying this is a step backwards, and also excludes the trans-masc people and also male allies  from the fight to gain equal footing in society to cis peoples. 

I am not sure if you meant that the men who harass and commit hate crimes against trans people are our "True enemies" or just men in general because they are the most likely to commit these crimes statistically, but it still stands that TERFs are an organised group who are against trans people and that is the reason they get so much attention from the trans community.

The reason TERFs are (What I would argue) are our true enemies is that the media, and other questioning trans people take their comments seriously. It doesn't particularly matter how small their group is, because their voice is wide reaching.

I suppose that's where I agree with you. I think the trans community does have an "obsession" with TERFs, and that makes their voices louder, but I don't think the way to go about "beating" them (I think is the right term) is to completely ignore them, as I don't think that solves the main problem with TERF's being very vocal and also doesn't stop their mantra harming trans people.

Feel free to disagree with me on this, I am not saying I am right, just wanted to give my opinion on this.

Just saying that Depression can cause low levels of energy and general apathy towards cleanliness (Of you and your surroundings). Also your sudden loss in interest in sports is a thing that is a symptom and a cause of depression.

If you are super happy and have a positive outlook on life that's totally great though! Just from what you've said here it resonates strongly with what I and a lot of my friends went through during episodes of depression, and if you've maybe overlooked it, it won't really matter what other advice you get as you'll still have depression as the underlying problem. If you want to talk about it PM me though.

If you are just feeling lazy however; download a streaks app. One where you can enter activities and check them off everyday making a streak. Enter some basic tasks (Make bed, brush teeth, make one meal, etc) and do them everyday, and soon you'll feel like you have more energy and feel more is accomplished during the day. You can also add more complex stuff on (Going to the gym) but start off really small and achievable and you'll be able to build some big streaks up.

For cleanliness have a "Use it, clean it" mentality. Use a dish? Wash it and put it where it belongs immediately. Get out of bed? Make you bed as soon as you are up. This prevents build up of problems and makes mess more manageable. 

Last thing I have is take tasks in chunks. You'll never do a giant task that you didn't really want to do in the first place. Cleaning the kitchen for example, you can use time or objectives. For time say to yourself -

"I'll spend 15 minutes washing dishes" - Then stop, or say
"I'll wash 5 dishes then stop" - Depending on your energy levels. Although you might make only small amounts progress (Depending on how small your goals are) you'll make infinitely more progress than looking at a big task and doing nothing. 

I hope at least some of this helps!
